steps.content: You walk through the carriage corridor, looking for additional clues near the spot where Clementine found the letter. Unfortunately, the corridor is spotless—there's not a single clue or speck of dust in sight.

You search with your head down, just like a mole, following the trail all the way to the connecting door leading to the second-class carriage. But then, you come to a halt. Someone is blocking the doorway, completely obstructing your path.
You look up. The first thing that catches your eye is a mass of disheveled hair.

The owner of that hair is slim, and she's currently leaning back with both feet firmly planted against the ground. She's pulling two old leather straps, her face flushed red—it seems like she's been locked in a losing battle with something.

steps.speaker: Attendant Allison
steps.content: Ma'am? Do you need any help?
The attendant notices the strange sight as well. But the moment she draws closer, the woman flinches as if some defense mechanism has been triggered.
Stop! Don't come any closer! I can do this! Don't touch it!
The protests tumble out one after another. Only now do you get a clear look at what she's referring to.

It appears to be a deep gray, oversized suitcase, nearly as tall as she is. It's been wedged firmly between the doorframe, a perfect fit in the worst way possible. Clearly, the suitcase was a little too much for the available space to handle. This exit's no good now.
Just how much luggage does she have? You briefly calculate the ratio between volume and travel duration, but the math simply doesn't add up, no matter what.

The woman stays silent. She releases the straps and pulls out a glass bottle from her pocket. A neat white label, covered in dense, printed instructions, is affixed to it. It looks more like laboratory equipment than something you'd carry on a trip.

steps.speaker: Attendant Allison
steps.content: Ma'am, what are you...?
The strange woman quickly measures the doorframe, then unscrews the cap and carefully applies the liquid to both sides. Her movements are precise, the coverage even.
Once she's finished, she stuffs the bottle back into her pocket, takes a deep breath, and grabs hold of the two worn straps once more.
She steps back again, then pulls hard.
Mmph...!
Her strength is surprising considering her slender frame—the suitcase actually moves.
<i>The doorframe groans from the friction, and a layer of dust gets shaken off. The suitcase inches its way into the carriage, agonizingly slow, but it is undeniably moving forward. What a triumph!

Unfortunately, just as the suitcase clears the doorframe, the straps snap. Inertia sends her stumbling forward, as for the suitcase... its weight had already tipped into the carriage, so it no longer had the support of the frame. And, just as expected, it comes toppling down toward her.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Watch out!
<i>You instinctively lunge forward and yank her to the side, but she drags you down with her. Both of you hit the floor. CRASH!

The straps snap, and the massive suitcase—nearly as tall as a person—crashes to the floor and bursts open. You catch a glimpse of several old Legend of the Star Realm discs and a few anatomy journals. Just then, a white shape springs loose, bouncing straight toward your face.

You instinctively reach out to catch it, but end up missing on your first try. A dull ache spreads around your temple. On the second attempt, you finally grab hold of the assailant. It's smooth to the touch, but the shape feels... odd.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What is this...?!
You look down. In your hand is a complete leg bone.
A few steps away, inside the opened suitcase, lies a nearly complete human skeleton that has been neatly arranged. The skull tilts to one side, the position it's in much more comfortable than yours.

steps.speaker: Attendant Allison
steps.content: AHHH! W-what is that?!
Vita! Leia!
She lunges at you and snatches the leg bone from your grasp.
Oh, thank goodness. The structure's intact, no cracks either... Don't worry, I'll put you right back next to Luke.
Hm? Wait... Dorothy's missing too. Where did she go...?
<i>Is she... talking to the bones?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Are these... skeleton models?
She raises her head instantly, her expression turning serious.
They're not models. They're specimens. I can show you Vita's bone density report if you'd like, but I need to find Dorothy first.

steps.speaker: Attendant Allison
steps.content: Bone density...? So they're all... real? An-and all these different names—don't tell me you named all of these bones?!
The attendant's voice trembles with each word, and she looks like she's about to faint any moment now.

steps.speaker: [Insert special portrait - Old sheriff's badge]
steps.content: Of course. 206 of them, to be exact, since that's the number of bones in a complete skeleton. Isn't that common knowledge?
Silence fills the air for several seconds. The attendant's hand trembles as she reaches for the call button.

steps.speaker: Attendant Allison
steps.content: Who... who even collects bones like this...?

The attendant points at the skeleton in horror. Her mouth opens and closes, yet the words seem to be stuck in her throat. At this rate, this woman will be thrown off the train before she can find her precious Vita, Leia, and Dorothy.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The monsters back away, allowing you to retreat further down the alley. The fog here is damp and cold, making the alley seem even more dark and sinister.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This skeleton has a label from the Judicial Forensic Research Institute. It should be a legitimate research specimen.
You point to the leg bone in her hands—a small tag can, in fact, be found on it.

The attendant leans in, her body still stiff. She scrutinizes the tag, and only then does she give a reluctant nod. She struggles to compose herself, her voice still trembling as she asks the woman to keep the specimens secure to avoid disturbing other passengers. Her professional training can only do so much for her in a situation like this.

With the shaken attendant sent on her way, you turn back to the owner of the luggage. She's already crouched on the floor, wholly absorbed in searching for scattered pieces. You catch her picking up a small white object from the carpet.

steps.speaker: Old Woman
steps.content: Oh my... Thank you, dear. Those are my dentures.
The old woman takes the white object from Forensica's hand without a second thought, deftly pops it into her mouth, and gives a satisfied smile.
The woman wrinkles her nose in distaste, wipes her hand with her clothes, and continues her search.
She's practically burying her face in the carpet, so engrossed in her search that she fails to notice what's right behind her—a small, pale bone resting atop her disheveled hair.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Excuse me, I think something fell on your head.
She frowns at you in confusion. You point to the top of her head again. She reaches up hesitantly, and the bone slides off, landing right in front of her.
Yes, that's it! Left pinky distal phalanx... My little Dorothy!

She cradles the tiny finger bone like some precious treasure, swiftly returning all the bones to their proper places. Her movements are proficient, the sequence methodical—clearly, this is not the first time she's had to reassemble a scattered skeleton.

She slams the suitcase shut with a bang, muttering about needing to find replacements for the worn-out straps... For the sake of everyone's peace of mind, you decide to lend her a spare belt from your own luggage.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Do you work at a forensic institute in the city? Next time... you might want to let the attendant know you're bringing items like this before boarding, otherwise it could lead to some very unnecessary misunderstandings—
Before you can finish, she suddenly springs to her feet and shoves a crumpled piece of paper into your hands.
Are you troubled by unexplained, corpse-related issues? Family or friends who died a suspicious death? If so, visit the StarRealm Unnatural Death Agency!
And now it's your turn to tilt your head in confusion.
<i>You uncrumple the piece of paper. It's a handwritten business card:

<color=#fb9259>"Problems left unsolved in life?
They might just be resolved in death!"</color>

Star Realm Unnatural Death Agency

Chief Coroner: Forensica
By the time you look up again, the woman named Forensica has already dragged her suitcase away.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...I really hope I never have to use this.
